test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 28 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Union Budget 2024-25 enhanced the limit of Mudra loans under the ‘Tarun’ category to _____ for entrepreneurs who have availed and successfully repaid previous loans.
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹20 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Budget 2024-25 increased the limit for Mudra loans under the 'Tarun' category to ₹20 lakh.
 
• This enhancement is aimed at providing greater financial assistance to entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid their previous loans.
 
• Mudra loans are part of the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), which was launched in April 2015.
 
• The 'Tarun' category is for loans above ₹10 lakh and up to ₹20 lakh.
 
• This initiative is expected to boost the growth of small businesses and startups in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)**

 
 
• Launched by the Government of India in April 2015 to provide loans to small and micro enterprises.
 
• MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency Ltd.
 
• The scheme offers loans under three categories: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹20 lakh).
 
• It aims to promote entrepreneurship among individuals and small businesses.
 
• The loans are provided by Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, Cooperative Banks, MFIs, and NBFCs.
 
 
 
• **Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS)**
 
 
• Launched to strengthen the credit delivery system and facilitate the flow of credit to the MSE sector.
 
• Provides credit guarantee for loans up to ₹2 crore.
 
• Helps small and micro enterprises in obtaining credit without the need for collateral security.
 
• Implemented by the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE).
 
 
 
• **Startup India Initiative**
 
 
• Launched by the Government of India on January 16, 2016.
 
• Aims to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and startups in the country.
 
• Offers benefits such as tax exemptions, simplified compliance, and fast-tracking of patent applications.
 
• Provides funding support through the Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) with a corpus of ₹10,000 crore.
 
 
 
• **Stand-Up India Scheme**
 
 
• Launched on April 5, 2016, to promote entrepreneurship among women and SC/ST communities.
 
• Provides bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore for setting up a greenfield enterprise.
 
• The scheme covers all branches of Scheduled Commercial Banks.
 
• Aims to facilitate at least two such projects per bank branch.
